name: Tree Traversals (DFS)
description: Visiting every node in a tree in a specific order. In-order (left, root, right) visits nodes in sorted order for BSTs. Pre-order (root, left, right) is used for copying/serializing trees. Post-order (left, right, root) is used for deletion or evaluating expressions.

examples.title: Example 1: In-Order Traversal (Sorted Order for BST)
examples.explanation: Recursive: base case null, visit left, process root, visit right. Iterative: push all left nodes, then pop and process, then go right. Both return [1,2,3,4,5] for a BST. Time O(n), Space O(h) for recursion stack or explicit stack.

examples.title: Example 2: Pre-Order Traversal (Root First)
examples.explanation: Pre-order processes root before children. Used for serializing a tree (root, then left subtree, then right subtree). Iterative version must push right child before left so left is popped first. Time O(n), Space O(h).

name: BST Validation
description: Checks if a binary tree satisfies the BST property: left subtree values < node value < right subtree values. Must validate that ALL nodes in left subtree are smaller, not just immediate children.

examples.title: Example 1: Recursive with Min/Max Bounds
examples.explanation: Each recursive call tracks valid range (min, max). Left child inherits same min but gets new max = parent.val. Right child inherits same max but gets new min = parent.val. Time O(n), Space O(h) for call stack.

examples.title: Example 2: In-Order Validation (Check Sorted Order)
examples.explanation: BST in-order traversal produces a sorted sequence. Track previous value during traversal; if current <= previous, it's invalid. Space O(1) extra besides call stack. Time O(n), Space O(h).

name: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA)
description: Finds the lowest (deepest) node that is an ancestor of two given nodes. In a BST, can be solved iteratively using BST ordering. In a general binary tree, use recursive DFS.

examples.title: Example 1: LCA in BST (Iterative)
examples.explanation: Leverages BST property: if both values are greater, go right; if both smaller, go left. The split point (one on each side) is the LCA. Time O(h), Space O(1).

examples.title: Example 2: LCA in General Binary Tree (Recursive)
examples.explanation: Recurse left and right. If both return non-null, current node is LCA (p and q are on different sides). If only one returns non-null, that's the LCA (both on same side, or one IS the LCA). Time O(n), Space O(h).

name: Maximum Depth & Height
description: Calculates the longest path from root to leaf (depth) or longest path between any two nodes (diameter). Foundation for many tree problems involving height, balance, or longest path.

examples.title: Example 1: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
examples.explanation: Recursive: max of left and right depths + 1 for current node. BFS: count levels. Both O(n) time. Recursive uses O(h) stack space, BFS uses O(width) queue space.

examples.title: Example 2: Diameter of Binary Tree
examples.explanation: Diameter = longest path between any two nodes. At each node, diameter = leftHeight + rightHeight. Track global max while computing heights. Time O(n), Space O(h).

name: Invert / Mirror Binary Tree
description: Swaps left and right children at every node. Classic problem that tests understanding of tree traversal order and recursion. Can be solved recursively or iteratively (BFS or DFS).

examples.title: Example 1: Recursive Invert
examples.explanation: Swap children, then recursively invert each subtree. Base case: null node returns null. Time O(n) — visits each node once. Space O(h) for call stack.

examples.title: Example 2: Iterative BFS Invert
examples.explanation: BFS: level-order, swap children at each level. DFS: use stack, swap and push children. Both achieve same result. Iterative avoids recursion depth limits for very deep trees. Time O(n), Space O(width) for BFS or O(h) for DFS.
